transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, it's really nice to meet you. 

I guess I'm here because... well, I've been doing some things lately that don't really make a lot of sense. Just at work and school mostly. I'm a bookkeeping clerk, and I really try to be a good employee, I promise, but lately I've been getting into these little habits that I know probably look a bit strange to other people. 

Like, I'll start lining up all the receipts in a big line across the floor. Or I'll catch myself just tapping the calculator, always in sets of nine. It's honestly a little embarrassing to talk about, because I know it sounds weird. The other day, I was just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I couldn't really put them down until someone walked by and asked if I was okay. 

I'm sure it's just stress or something minor, right? I hope it's okay that I came in to talk to you about it. Is that the sort of thing you can help me with?

When you're doing these things—like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator in sets of nine—do you feel like you want to stop, or do you feel driven to keep doing them even though you know they might seem odd to others?

Um... that's a really good question. I guess... I haven't really thought about it quite like that. 

I don't know if I feel driven, exactly? It's not like I'm forcing myself to do it or anything intense like that. It's more just... I just sort of find myself doing it, almost like I'm just zoning out for a minute. I don't really try to stop because I don't always realize I'm doing it until, you know, I notice someone might be watching. Then I stop right away, I promise. 

I really hope that doesn't sound too strange... I mean, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.

When you're doing these things like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, do you feel any anxiety, worry, or uncomfortable thoughts beforehand that the tapping or organizing helps to relieve? Or do they just happen more automatically without that kind of mental discomfort driving them?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I feel anxious or worried beforehand. I promise I don't have any, like, bad thoughts or anything uncomfortable that I'm trying to get rid of. I really try to keep a positive attitude at work! 

It really is just... like you said, more automatic. I just kind of space out and my hands are just doing it. It's honestly just a silly, mindless habit, really, not because I'm upset or stressed in that moment. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope that's a good sign that I'm not anxious about it. Does that help answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How much do these habits bother you or get in the way of your work or daily life? Are they causing you any real problems, or do they feel pretty harmless overall?

Um... well, I really try to make sure they don't get in the way. I always want to do a good job, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... they might be causing a little bit of an issue. 

It's really embarrassing to admit this, because I don't want you to think I'm a bad worker or a bad student or anything, but... I actually failed an important course module recently. And at work, um... my ledgers have started coming back with some pretty serious errors. I've even had to ask my coworkers for help because I just... I can't seem to reliably finish the work that used to be totally routine for me. 

I feel terrible about it, I really do. I promise I'm trying my absolute best to get back on track and be helpful at the office. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right. Is it normal to struggle with that kind of stuff sometimes?

When you're tapping the calculator or holding your hands up in the air, does it feel like your muscles are just moving on their own, almost like a twitch or jerk? Or does it feel more like you're deliberately doing an action, even if you're not fully aware of it?

Um... well, it definitely doesn't feel like a twitch or a jerk. I promise I have full control over my body, it's not like a spasm or anything scary like that. 

I guess... it's more like I'm doing it deliberately, even though, like I said, I kind of zone out. It's just... I started doing these things that, well, I know they don't make a lot of sense. Like the receipts on the floor, or the calculator thing... or, um, sometimes I'll just be standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air. I don't really know why I do it, I just sort of stay like that until someone walks by and asks if I'm okay. 

I know it sounds a little odd when I say it out loud... I really hope it doesn't make me sound too weird or like I'm trying to be disruptive. I'm really not! I just... I came in to see you because I wanted to figure out why I'm doing these things at work and school. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.

Before you start tapping the calculator or arranging the receipts, do you ever feel a buildup of tension, pressure, or an uncomfortable sensation in your body—like something inside you is telling you that you need to do it to make things feel right or complete?

Oh, um, no... no, definitely not. I don't feel any kind of pressure or tension building up like that. I promise I don't have any weird feelings inside telling me I absolutely *have* to do it. That sounds really intense, and I'm definitely not trying to, like, fix anything to make it feel right or perfect. 

It really is just... well, like I mentioned before, I just sort of space out and it happens. There's no buildup at all. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm hoping it means it's not as bad since I'm not feeling all that physical pressure you mentioned. Am I answering that right for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.
When you're NOT doing these things—like when you're not tapping or arranging things—do you feel okay, or do you feel like something is missing or incomplete until you do them again?

Um, no, I feel totally okay when I'm not doing them. I definitely don't feel like anything is missing or, um, incomplete or anything like that. 

I actually really prefer when I'm just doing my normal work, you know? Like entering the data or studying for my classes. I don't miss doing the weird stuff at all. I really try to just focus on being a good employee and a good student. 

I hope that's the right answer? Like, I hope it's a good sign that I don't feel like I *need* to be doing those things all the time. I just want to get back to my normal routine and do a good job for everyone. Does that sound like a positive thing to you?

When you're tapping the calculator in sets of nine or holding your hands up by the copier, do these movements happen very quickly and suddenly, almost like little bursts? I know it sounds really strange, and I'm so sorry if it's hard to understand. I just... Is it okay that it happens slowly like that? Does that help you figure out what's going on?

Right before you do one of these things—like before you start tapping the calculator or lining up the receipts—do you ever feel an irresistible urge or a sudden need to do it, even if you try to resist?

Um, no, definitely not an irresistible urge. I don't feel any kind of sudden need like that at all. I know you're trying to figure out if I'm, like, compelled to do it, but I promise I'm not. I don't feel like I *have* to do it, and I'm definitely not fighting against it or trying to resist it. 

It really is just... I don't know, it just happens. I just sort of space out and start doing it. There's no big urge right before it starts.

When you're doing these things like tapping or holding your hands up, do they feel like movements that are happening to you—like something your body is doing on its own—or do they feel like actions that you are choosing to do, even if you're not thinking about why?

Um, well, it's definitely not like my body is just doing it on its own. I'm not, like, out of control or anything scary like that. I'm choosing to do it, I guess. It's just... I'm choosing to do it without really thinking about why. 

Like I was saying before, I just sort of space out and start doing these things that don't make sense. Like lining the receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or... or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I'm okay. I am doing it, it's just... it's just really weird, I know.

Does it make sense that I'm choosing to do it, even if I don't know why? Is that a better answer than if my body was just doing it on its own?

When you're doing these things, like tapping the calculator or holding your hands up by the copier, are they the same simple movements repeated over and over again? Or are they more complex actions that look like they might have a purpose, even though you're not sure why you're doing them?

Um, they're definitely more... complex, I think. Like, they look like they have a purpose, maybe? It's not just like my finger twitching on a button or something simple like that. 

Like when I line the receipts up across the floor, I'm, you know, placing them down in a specific way. Or when I'm tapping the calculator, it's specifically in sets of nine. And holding my hands up by the copier... it's a whole posture, you know? I just stay like that until someone comes by and asks if I'm okay. 

It's not just random jerking around. It looks like I'm doing a task, even though I know it doesn't make any sense to anyone else. I mean, I know it's not normal clerk behavior, and that's why I came in. I really want to be doing things the right way. Does that help? Is it better that they look like they have a purpose, rather than just being random twitches?

When you're doing these things—like tapping the calculator in sets of nine or lining up the receipts—do you feel like you're following some kind of pattern or rule that you need to follow? For example, does it have to be exactly nine taps, or exactly a certain way, or can you do it differently?

Um, no, not really like a strict rule or anything. I mean, I guess I said sets of nine before, but... it's not like I'm counting them out perfectly every single time, or like something bad will happen if it's only eight taps, you know? 

It's not a rigid pattern that I'm obsessed with following. It's just sort of... how it happens when I space out. I don't feel forced to do it exactly one way. I could probably do it differently if I really thought about it, but like I said, I'm just not really thinking about it when it happens. 

I'm not, like, crazy strict about it having to be perfect. I know that would probably sound pretty bad, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm not stuck in some weird set of rules. I'm really trying to be flexible and normal. Is that a good thing, that I don't have strict rules for it?

When you're tapping the calculator or lining up the receipts, do these movements look like they serve some kind of purpose or function—like you're actually accomplishing something—even though you know logically they don't make sense? Or do they feel more pointless and just... repetitive for no reason at all?

Um, well... I guess they look like they might have a purpose, maybe? Like, to someone just glancing over, it might look like I'm doing real clerk work. 

When I'm lining the receipts across the floor, I mean, I'm organizing them, right? Just... not in a way that actually helps with the bookkeeping. And standing by the copier with my hands up... well, I guess that one is a little harder to explain away. I just kind of stay there until someone asks if I'm okay. 

But I'm really not trying to be disruptive or anything. I know it doesn't make sense, and that's why I'm here. I want to be doing actual, useful work. I don't want people to think I'm just doing pointless, crazy things. It's better if it looks like I'm at least trying to accomplish something, right? I'm really hoping we can fix this so I can just be a normal, productive worker again.

It's not like my body is, you know, forcing me to finish it. Like I said, I came in because I know these things—lining the receipts up across the floor, the tapping the calculator, or just standing by the copier with my hands up—I know they don't make sense for work or school. I'm really trying to be cooperative and do things the right way.
